prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a verified physical discovery in which theory and experiment fit together unusually cleanly. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model (2011) predicted a non-obvious band structure, flat bands at a specific twist angle, and the 2018 experiments of Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle. Many independent groups have since reproduced the phase diagram in several devices and moire systems, and spectroscopy (STM, ARPES-type probes) supports the band-structure picture, which is the kind of quantitative theory-to-spectra link I trust. It created a tunable platform for correlated quantum matter and echoes the graphene lesson that experiment can overturn what theorists believed. A theory-plus-experiment trio is a natural structure for the prize.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is maturity of interpretation. The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved and the field is moving fast, with moire TMDs and other platforms that could reshape the narrative. The credited names also omit the first experimental authors (Cao, Fatemi) and earlier theory precursors such as Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, so the attribution would be criticised whichever three or two names are chosen. If the committee decides that eight years is too early, a more mature candidate such as optical lattice clocks (B018) or topological insulators (B034) is the safer choice.

responses.point: Pearce ranks twisted bilayer graphene seventh, defers to condensed-matter colleagues, and judges the timing possible but perhaps early because the superconducting mechanism is debated and junior team members are uncredited.
responses.response: I accept the credit concern but disagree that an open pairing mechanism makes the discovery early. The Nobel criterion is a robust, independently confirmed phenomenon, and the existence of the flat-band-driven correlated insulators and superconducting domes has been confirmed across many laboratories and techniques. The mechanism of high-Tc cuprates was never settled when they were honoured. I agree that experimental credit beyond Jarillo-Herrero is a real weakness and would want the committee to confirm that the group-leader convention is applied consistently. I would keep Bistritzer, since your two-name version drops the person who co-authored the decisive prediction.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks first as a clean two-person case (Katori, Ye): reproduced worldwide, timely, with a pending redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I find the attribution argument for B018 persuasive and I would not call it incremental. Where I differ is on what is new in nature. The clock is a superb instrument with a clear credit story, but its novelty sits closer to the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and the discovery content is a performance record, whereas twisted bilayer graphene revealed a new state of matter. I keep B018 as my first alternative because its maturity and attribution are better than those of my first choice.

responses.point: Johansson ranks circuit QED first on its foundational role in superconducting processors, and notes it complements the 2025 prize, while admitting the Girvin versus Blais allocation problem and proximity to his own field.
responses.response: I respect that Johansson flagged his own proximity. My reservations are that four credited names cannot fit three places without dropping either a lead theorist or a lead experimentalist, and that the committee that I chaired just recognised superconducting circuits in 2025, so a second award from the same family so soon is hard to defend against a condensed-matter discovery with no such overlap. I would not rule it out if the allocation could be settled on the proposal-plus-strong-coupling pair.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks optical lattice clocks first for stability, independent reproduction in many laboratories and clear credit, and places topological insulators seventh because the credited set omits Bernevig, Zhang, Fu and Moore.
responses.response: I agree with her on the topological-insulator attribution problem and it is the reason I keep B034 only as a second alternative, not as my preferred choice. The list leaves out Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the 2016 prize overlaps in subject. On the clocks I agree the credit is cleaner than for most candidates.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the twisted bilayer graphene interpretation stable enough, given the unresolved pairing mechanism.
How to treat experimental credit for Cao, Fatemi and others, and the precursor theory of Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, within a three-person limit.
Whether to prefer a more mature candidate (B018 or B034) if the committee wants distance from 2016 and 2025 prize topics.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I know DFT and moire/ARPES-type work in the field generally, but the profile lists no collaboration with MacDonald, Bistritzer or Jarillo-Herrero. I chaired the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits, which bears on the B008 discussion but is not a personal connection to any candidate.
